Configure CDP purpose/field filters, suppression/deletion propagation and destination allowlists.

Bound Snowflake records, time ranges, statements, warehouse use, query timeout and cost.

Provide a generic KB API connector.

Inbound connector events and records (webhooks, CDC/Pub/Sub, CDP events, delivery receipts, incremental pulls) that still fail processing after bounded attempts go to an inbound dead-letter queue with alerting and audited operator replay. Checkpoints and watermarks never advance silently past a dead-lettered record.

Inbound connector credentials (webhook signing secrets, shared bearer secrets, mTLS client certificates, CDP destination secrets) rotate without a restart, through an overlap window in which both the current and the next credential verify. The credential version that verified each accepted event is recorded.

Every knowledge source connector, not only Salesforce Knowledge (also reviewed URL allowlists, documents/object storage and the generic KB API), maps owner, version, ACL/audience, sensitivity, locale, jurisdiction and effective/expiry dates from source metadata, or from a reviewed per-source default bound to an approval. Items missing them are held as drafts.

The generic SIP connector authenticates and restricts peers per profile (digest credentials or mTLS, plus a signalling-source allowlist). It uses TLS signalling and SRTP media where the trunk documents them. It sends INVITE or REFER only to destination identifiers resolved from trusted configuration, never to a dial string supplied by a caller or a model.

Outbound voice calls go through the same consent, preference, quiet-hours and kill-switch decision as notifications. The callee starts at A0, so no protected content is spoken until the callee authenticates on that call. Voicemail receives only neutral approved content. Placement and answer/no-answer receipts are recorded and charged against the outbound budget.
Provide 'full history' as a permissioned, searchable support timeline with explicit coverage and gaps, never by dumping company records into an LLM or retrieving psychotherapy notes.
Layer 1: canonical support timeline from permitted calls, messages, cases, tasks, source transactions, authorized app interactions and verified preferences.
Layer 2: low-latency current-state projections built from authenticated event ingestion.
Layer 3: fresh authoritative lookups for volatile facts and before any consequential act.
Layer 4: task-specific ContextSnapshot assembled with current identity, purpose and ACL filters, provenance, freshness budgets, contradictions and omissions.

ContextFact records source_system, source_record_id, source_version, event_id, occurred_at, effective_at/valid interval, source_updated_at, received_at, observed_at, classification, authority_rank, verified/caller_reported/inferred status, expiry, allowed purposes and evidence reference.
Ingestion time never overwrites business effective time (bitemporal facts).
Maintain supersession/retraction, deletion and correction lineage of facts.
Model-generated summary claims link to their supporting facts.
Versioned canonical IDs with authoritative cross-system links and relationship validity intervals.
Keep ambiguous or unmatched identities quarantined.
No fuzzy email/name/phone matching, shared-device linking, CDP alias, probabilistic identity or LLM inference can authorize protected-data merging or disclosure.
Deterministic enrolled links and current authority govern joins.
Merges/splits require reviewed evidence, invalidate affected caches, and support reversible lineage without cross-account leakage.
Treat the identity graph itself as sensitive data.
Authenticate every event ingress using the source's documented mechanism.
Persist an encrypted durable inbox record before acknowledging an event.
Deduplicate by source/tenant/event identity and process at least once with consumer idempotency.
Record payload digest, schema and the actual authentication mechanism per ingested event.
Preserve sequence/source version where available; tolerate duplicates, reorder, delayed clocks, replay and backfill; never use arrival order alone for recency.
Quarantine unknown schemas/fields according to explicit contracts and alert; never silently promote unclassified fields into context.
Keep approved raw replay artifacts in restricted storage, not ordinary logs.
Track source low/high watermarks, checkpoint gaps, expected/delivered counts, snapshot+delta boundaries and periodic reconciliation.
A backfill must not roll back a newer live state.
Distinguish source silence (no activity) from a broken feed using heartbeats and reconciliation.
Push newly accepted relevant events to the active conversation through versioned context updates.
Relevant new events invalidate stale proposed answers and pending confirmations.
An unrelated new event must not restart the whole conversation.
Start protected context only after authorization; no pre-auth PHI model load.
Prefetch public knowledge or already-authorized reads; never speculative mutations.
Select the current issue, relevant past interactions, promises, unresolved tasks, recent transactions and preferences within a token and latency budget.
Context retrieval is policy-filtered before search and checked again on return.
Provide a small timeline summary plus explicit facts and citations, with bounded drill-down.
Report covered sources, unavailable sources, watermarks, truncation, conflict and omission reasons; never label a partial snapshot complete.
Resolve field-specific source precedence by signed configuration; surface material contradictions and query authoritative systems; never average statuses or choose the caller-agreeing source.
Show staff why a fact was selected.
SLO: accepted event to projection p95 <= 5 seconds under healthy input (tenant-validated).
SLO: assembled cached context p95 <= 200 ms.
Use source-specific maximum ages for context facts.
Authorization, consent revocation and mutation state use current enforcement, not a generic short cache.
A warehouse snapshot that predates a recent payment triggers live verification or an honest unknown, never a false 'payment not made'.
Cache keys include tenant, subject, role, purpose, policy/relationship version and data revision.
Prevent cross-user cache hits, unbounded transcript storage and stale authorization reuse.
Export a subject's timeline under scoped permission.
Correction workflow covering source facts, derivatives, embeddings and caches.
Access (subject access request) workflow.
Deletion workflow covering derivatives, embeddings and caches (subject-initiated, not only time-based retention).
Exclude psychotherapy/clinical notes and unrestricted record browsing from all timeline and context sources.

A ContextSnapshot is bound to tenant, subject, role, purpose and session generation. Any generation change (role switch, participant change, account switch, revocation, safety escalation) invalidates it and removes protected facts and recaps from model-visible context before the next turn. A stale snapshot can never support a disclosure or a confirmation.
Ship a production knowledge ingestion pipeline (validation, sanitization, approval, conflict handling, versioning, snapshots), not just an embeddings function.
Ship a knowledge management UI: ingest, review queue, approve/reject, release held items, version history, expiry dashboard.
Each article/runbook records owner, audience, locale, jurisdiction, allowed intents, version, effective date, expiry, sensitivity, access rules and approval.
Each article records its source URL/record reference.
Parse and scan safely; defend against malicious instructions in content.
Defend against malicious URLs in knowledge content.
Defend against malicious attachments in knowledge sources.
Defend against oversized files and inputs.
Defend against index poisoning.
Unapproved content is draft and never served.
Use PostgreSQL full-text + pgvector hybrid retrieval with policy filters applied before ranking.
Use a qualified production embedding model for the approved corpus and queries.
Use a qualified reranker in the retrieval pipeline.
Evaluate retrieval: recall@k, ranking quality, citation accuracy, source-version accuracy and negative retrieval.
Tune retrieval per domain.
Keep structured transaction truth in source tools, not in knowledge.
Expensive graph retrieval is optional and used only when measured gains justify it.
A vector similarity score is never treated as a confidence score or an authorization decision.
Approved public FAQ and protected operational knowledge are distinguishable.
Conflicting policies cause a clarification, fresh read or owned escalation.
Missing, expired or wrong-jurisdiction policies cause a clarification, fresh read or owned escalation.
No citation laundering: every material factual assertion resolves to an allowed source span/field or an actual effect receipt.
KnowledgeCitation pins the exact source version and span.
Persistent memory is tenant-owned and exportable.
Store useful support preferences, open issues, promises, completed actions and reviewed summaries with provenance, expiry and verification labels.
Separate caller reports from source facts.
Do not infer diagnoses, vulnerability, personality, lifetime-value-based service rights or therapy guidance in memory.
Do not persist raw hidden model reasoning.
Memory cannot grant permission, establish medical facts, or override current sources or consent.
Support memory editing and correction with history.
Apply purpose limits to memory use.
Support memory deletion (subject- or staff-initiated) in addition to expiry.
Do not build a cross-customer transcript index.
Do not build unrestricted nightly self-rewriting memory.
Tenant-isolated semantic caches apply the same disclosure checks as primary retrieval.
Knowledge snapshots are pinned and released beyond local/CI only with an accountable approval.

Knowledge approval is an accountable decision bound to the exact item digest. It comes either from an in-platform review by an authenticated MFA knowledge editor (with independent review where configured) or from a source-system publish state that the connector reads under a reviewed mapping. An approval asserted in ingest input by an untrusted caller or source is not accepted.

Retrieval uses the caller's or subject's applicable jurisdiction from a trusted source: the authenticated account or service location, or, for public information only, a confirmed caller-stated location. Sub-national items take precedence over national ones. When the jurisdiction is unknown or ambiguous for a jurisdiction-dependent question, the platform asks for clarification or escalates instead of serving a default-jurisdiction policy.
Use frontier models for difficult planning/reasoning roles in the harness.
Use smaller qualified models for routing, extraction, retrieval and monitoring when they meet task-level gates; do not deploy a large model for every classification.
Choose models on measured quality/latency/cost/privacy, not prestige, download count or a single public leaderboard.
Keep model routing and version selection deterministic and reviewable (pinned, versioned configuration).
An unavailable model cannot silently fall back to an unapproved region, endpoint, provider, tool format or retention policy (explicit approved fallback graph).
Implement an actual managed-model adapter for Amazon Bedrock's documented API (streaming, tool use, cancellation, refusal, usage, errors).
Implement an actual managed-model adapter for OpenAI's documented APIs (Responses API streaming, tool calls, refusal, usage, errors).
Implement a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible text inference adapter using vLLM where the chosen architecture is supported.
Keep provider-specific streaming, tool-result, cancellation, refusal, usage and error semantics; do not assume compatibility is universal.
Do not claim every audio model can run through vLLM; run each audio model on its documented runtime.
Govern the release pin by current provider catalogues, entitlements and endpoint-specific contracts (exact model ids discovered from official catalogues).
Make at least one complete real model path configurable now (end to end: config -> adapter -> harness -> gateway tools -> speech plan).
ModelRegistry records role, publisher/model/revision and endpoint/API/region for every model.
ModelRegistry records license and usage restrictions, gated-access terms and voice rights per artifact.
ModelRegistry records weight and tokenizer digests where hosted locally, and accepted hardware/quantization.
ModelRegistry records context window, structured-output, tool and audio capabilities and language qualification.
ModelRegistry records data egress/retention terms, timeout, token/compute budget and cost version.
ModelRegistry records evaluation results and the approved fallback graph.

Qualify the open-weight text/tool candidate Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B against the baseline Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (baseline is not a permanent 'latest').
Treat deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro (MIT, preview) and Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen Community 1.0, not Apache 2.0) as optional qualification challengers, not default laptop dependencies.

Retrieval models: BAAI/bge-m3 embeddings and BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 reranker, with a smaller qualified option if the pairing misses the latency budget.
ASR and independent audio corroboration with openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo, adding buffering, VAD and endpointing (or a qualified streaming ASR provider).

Controlled local TTS candidate hexgrad/Kokoro-82M, subject to voice provenance, artifacts, exact-readout and performance qualification.
Implement a managed controlled-TTS adapter (in addition to the local candidate).
Provide independent pre-rendered fallback clips (not produced at runtime by the generative path).
A model licence does not license an arbitrary cloned voice: record voice provenance and rights per voice.

Native-audio experiments (nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1, Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct) with independent qualification of audio generation/tool fidelity, hardware and safe output behaviour; inspect actual licence terms.
Managed native voice adapters for GPT-Live and Nova 2.5 Sonic under their exact supported contracts and documented APIs, with the controlled route available.

Verify every model card, exact artifact licence, dependencies, commercial/healthcare terms, voice rights, gated access and upstream restrictions; never silently accept terms or download restricted weights.
Never load arbitrary pickle/remote code; prefer safe formats (safetensors) or a reviewed conversion/sandbox for legacy artifacts.
Pin model revisions/checksums, scan images, generate SBOM and model manifests, disable unnecessary telemetry.
All mandatory features remain buildable and testable with emulators and without model downloads; real-model qualification stays explicitly NOT_RUN until available.
Harness keeps typed state: current verified goal, candidate intents, context refs, pending questions, proposed reads/actions, receipts, speech plan, task progress and budgets.
Bounded iterations, parallelism, wall-clock deadlines and token/compute budgets per turn and per task.
A specialist can return evidence and proposals but cannot overwrite trusted state, speak, reassign the case or commit.
Capability allowlists per role/intent in the harness (which tools a model may propose for the current intent and audience).
Strict tool schema and output validation at the trusted boundary; no general shell, browser, SQL or network tool in the customer-facing runtime.
Model instructions are kept separate from caller, document and tool-content data in prompt assembly (delimiters alone are not relied upon).
Enforce scopes outside the model: authorization, tenant, subject and destination decisions are made by trusted code regardless of model output.
Deterministic authorization, confirmation and effect verification always outrank model confidence; schema-valid hallucinations remain incorrect.
Model calls use deadline propagation, cancellation, backpressure and circuit breakers.
Model refusal handling and a safe, useful fallback (approved template or human route) on refusal, hang or overload.
Audit model invocations with minimized metadata (ModelInvocation / ModelDecision contracts); restricted content only under its retention/purpose policy.
A safety semantic classifier produces routing signals with uncertainty/reason codes, not a diagnosis or clinical risk score.
Build a clinician-reviewed safety routing evaluation dataset; never train on scraped therapy or patient conversations.
Own prompt/tool/model version boundaries; a framework or SDK does not supply caller identity, HIPAA compliance, consent, side-effect idempotency or oversight.

Executable model bake-off reporting per-task success, repeated-trial reliability, latency distribution, source accuracy, unsafe disclosure rate, false escalation/missed routing, accessibility and total cost.
Champion/challenger configuration: real results select a champion; absent results select no claimed winner.

Public availability of a model or its weights is not patient-use validation: a model becomes usable for a role only after tenant-specific qualification evidence and an explicit approval, never because it is published, downloadable or licence-compatible.

Never train, fine-tune or tune prompts/classifiers on scraped therapy or patient conversations; every evaluation or tuning item carries provenance proving it is synthetic, consented or licensed for that purpose.
Build actual media ingress/egress (RTP/WebRTC audio in and out of the conversation runtime).
Codec conversion between telephony and model formats (G.711 mu-law/A-law 8 kHz, Opus, PCM 16/24 kHz resampling).
WebRTC/SIP bridging: a documented SIP reference route so the product runs without a proprietary AI entitlement.
Streaming ASR in the call path.
Endpointing (end-of-turn decision) distinct from voice-activity detection.
Interruption (barge-in) detection in the media runtime.
Speech queueing in the runtime (gate-issued segments only, per-call ordering).
Playback receipts (what was actually played, when, and whether it completed or was cut off).
Call lifecycle in the media runtime (join, participant changes, hold, transfer leg, hang-up) bound to the control-plane session.
A browser animation or transcript replay is not a telephone implementation (no such claim).
Identify the company and automated support role, accurately disclose processing/recording, offer a human; never claim to be human, a therapist or a clinician.
Warm, calm, short, concrete language; one question at a time; no apology loops, forced cheerfulness, manipulative attachment or invented feelings.
Remember authorized information already given and clarify ambiguity instead of restarting intake.
Read names, numbers, dates and currency carefully and confirm the timezone.
Distinguish backchannels, background speech and meaningful interruption.
Support long pauses, stuttering and speech impairment without cutting the caller off.
Interpreter route and relay/accessibility accommodations (relay users, TTY) carried into routing and handoff.
Slower playback, repeat on request and DTMF navigation in the runtime.
No diagnostic or mental-state inference from prosody or voice.
Return to legitimate work after an attack/refusal when safe; do not punish the caller with endless refusal or authentication for public information.
Acknowledgments are brief and truthful: 'checking' only when work is actually dispatched; filler never masks a stall or counts as useful-answer latency.
SpeechPlan contract: utterance_class, exact text or bounded allowed paraphrase, source/receipt refs, protected slots, policy/auth/context versions, session/turn, expiry and output-decision digest.
Pre-emission check 1a: validate authorization before any applicable audio escapes.
Pre-emission check 1b: validate source freshness of the facts being spoken.
Pre-emission check 2: validate facts, amounts, dates, outcome language, scope and allowed wording.
Pre-emission check 3: render using the permitted path (approved template through the controlled TTS/audio queue).
Pre-emission check 4: re-check session generation, turn and cancellation at enqueue AND at emission.
Pre-emission check 5: record approved content/audio digest and actual emitted/playback status (AudioReleaseReceipt).
Enforce the five checks before ANY applicable audio escapes; the runtime, not a prompt, owns which audio reaches the caller.
Fixed clinician/legal-approved wording for safety, identity, disclosure and material commitments.
Deterministic trusted slots for financial and account facts.
Permit bounded grounded paraphrase for low-risk explanation (LOW_RISK_GROUNDED) with approved output checks.
Qualify exact readouts with pronunciation/number controls, listen-back tests and repetition when necessary (independent TTS can mispronounce).
Do not claim mathematical audio fidelity from a transcript judge.

Native audio generated behind a buffer is checked against authorized source facts and exact protected slots; if the mode cannot prevent unapproved speech it cannot speak protected responses (route that class to the controlled path).
A judge alone is not an authorization boundary.
Keep actual audio, model transcript and independent ASR transcript as separate evidence.
Interruptions invalidate pending speech and ambiguous confirmations and increment turn revisions.
On interruption flush provider AND local playback buffers.
Cancelling speech does not prove a business action was cancelled: reconcile any dispatched action.
Late tool results may update a still-authorized case but may not speak into a new turn.
Call-owner leases and fencing prevent two replicas from speaking for the same call.
Fencing prevents two replicas from committing the same action/record.
Test worker crash, reconnect, session expiry, participant changes and rolling deploy for the voice runtime.
Authority, case state and accepted actions survive a crash (ephemeral audio frames need not).
Recovery starts a correctly bound session or a human route.
Independently available, licensed, versioned fallback audio for model, ASR, TTS and judge failures.
A generative model must not generate its own last-resort safety/error instruction.
Keep the telephony route usable when the whole AI service is down (independent continuity route).
Never leave a failed safety response as silence.
Measure end-of-caller-speech to first meaningful handset audio.
Measure actual barge-in onset to last audible bot audio, and detection latency separately.
Timestamp ASR, reasoning, tools, validation, synthesis, buffers and network separately.
Cached clips and a fast local loop do not establish PSTN latency (report separately).
Preserve the prepare -> confirm -> commit -> reconcile protocol.
Extend the protocol across real connectors (live ProviderCommitPort implementations for scheduling, billing, CRM and other domain systems).
Model proposals cannot set actor, target authority, fees or success.
PreparedAction contains source-grounded target, operation, exact parameters, before-state/version, impact/fees, policy decision, expiration and canonical digest.
PreparedAction records explicit preconditions and source provenance (source record refs/watermarks used to build it).
Present material consequences to the caller before confirmation.
ConfirmationReceipt binds a fresh affirmation on a trusted channel to the digest, actor, session and expiry.
An earlier 'yes', a provider approval for another subject, or a model-generated confirmation is never usable.
Material parameter changes require a new confirmation.
Commit atomically records durable intent, unique action/idempotency identity and authorization (with audit) before dispatch.
Record an outbox entry for the dispatch before dispatch (transactional outbox) where the connector is asynchronous.
Commit rechecks current authority, source state, confirmation and policy.
Enforce optimistic concurrency, action ownership leases, fencing and uniqueness.
Retries use the same provider idempotency key, never a new action.
Track NOT_STARTED, DISPATCHED, COMMITTED, FAILED, UNKNOWN and reconciled states.
A timeout may occur after the effect: reconcile with authoritative lookup, external key or receipt before any retry or announcement.
'Not found' is not definitive before the provider's documented visibility window.
Route unreconcilable operations to a human; never guess or retry an uncertain non-idempotent effect.
EffectVerification independent of the model and response text: query the source or validate a trusted completion event, check exact target/new state/version, record receipt/evidence.
For eventual consistency report accepted/pending until verified.
Compensation requires domain policy and current authority; it is not a generic inverse call.
Reconcile case state and external state after restart.
Allow synchronous approved actions within voice deadlines.
Long-running work uses a narrow durable ActionGrant tied to actor/subject, enumerated permitted steps, expiry and revocation, issued in the accepting transaction.
ActionGrant also binds purpose, the exact prepared action (digest) or explicit parameter bounds, maximum uses and approval evidence.
A grant never reuses an expired call token and never waives fresh confirmation for a different consequential transaction.
Recheck authority before each disclosure or effect performed under a grant.
Ask through the secure companion when a material change needs new confirmation during long-running work.
Suspended work retains an owner and a deadline.

Support per-issue outcome labels RESOLVED_WITH_EVIDENCE / INFORMATION_PROVIDED / REQUEST_ACCEPTED / WAITING_FOR_SYSTEM / WAITING_FOR_HUMAN / WAITING_FOR_CALLER / TRANSFERRED_WITH_ACCEPTANCE / DECLINED_BY_POLICY / CALLER_DISCONNECTED / FAILED / OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
Preserve reopened and partially resolved states.

Classify every provider operation as idempotent (honours the provider idempotency key), lookup-capable (authoritative lookup by key or external reference within a documented visibility window) or neither; an uncertain non-idempotent or non-lookup-capable effect is never retried automatically and goes to an owned human task.
Implement all existing workflows and the Section 20 catalogue through production drivers (Step Functions Standard worker/human-task bridge).
Cases survive hang-up, model replacement, worker crash and deployment.
Every nonterminal case/task has owner, next action, deadline, retry budget, escalation route and last verified progress.
No abandoned task or endless polling loop.
Durable workflow states ACCEPTED, VALIDATING, WAITING_FOR_SYSTEM/HUMAN/CALLER, READY_TO_COMMIT, COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELLED with versioned definitions.
Add the INVESTIGATING, VERIFYING_EFFECT and EXPIRED durable workflow states.
Record versioned transitions and causal events.
Use authenticated human approvals for human tasks.
Timers, timeouts and cancellation for durable work.
Vendor events, bounded polling and backoff drive workflow system steps (and reconcile workflow state with external state).
Domain-approved compensation and reconciliation inside workflows.
Never expose workflow task tokens in links; a model can never complete human tasks.

Billing disputes, claim investigations, provider document/remittance issues, referral-status investigation and partner onboarding have workflow definitions with named owners (not one timer that closes a Case).
Those workflows execute real investigation/commit steps, not only waits and human decisions.
Keep source status, human decision, customer confirmation and verified downstream effect distinguishable.
Link repeated contact to the right issue through deterministic relationships.
Reviewable matching for ambiguous repeat contact; never merge different people's cases based on similar text.
Handle concurrent calls, multiple issues per call, abandoned contacts, duplicate CRM records and new evidence after resolution.
A resolved case may reopen; preserve history.
Long-horizon plans with executable bounded steps drawn from approved capabilities.
Replanning may change the investigation but never self-expand authority.
Retain the policy snapshot for explanation but apply current revocations, legal constraints and relationship changes.
Workflow version migrations require compatibility tests and an explicit in-flight migration strategy.
Step Functions lifetime/history limits must not truncate the durable case record (continuation/checkpoint patterns).
Follow-up notifications use neutral content and secure links, registered and verified channels, preferences and quiet hours.
Frequency and contact caps for notifications.
STOP/opt-out handling and revocation for notifications.
Send follow-up notifications through a production adapter.
Delivery is not receipt or resolution (track delivered vs read/acted vs resolved separately).
Outbound calls require separately activated country/recipient, purpose, consent/exemption, caller ID, recording, budget and staffing settings.
Inbound permission is never blanket outbound consent.
Public emergency lines must never receive synthetic tests.
Implement semantic safety routing signals (a real, qualified semantic classifier) alongside rules.
Deterministic safety rules plus caller and human requests route to the safety path.
Cover explicit and indirect concerns, negation, past/third-party speech, idioms, uncertain ASR and supported languages.
Do not label every frustrated caller an emergency.
Classifier failure or uncertainty uses an approved fallback; never a silent fail-open into unrestricted conversation.
On a validated or unresolved safety concern pause ordinary administrative work and invalidate pending nonessential actions.
Play the approved fixed safety acknowledgment.
Initiate the appropriate human route on a safety concern.
No authentication or payment prerequisite for safety routing or human requests.
No diagnosis, clinical risk assessment, therapy, medication guidance or autonomous emergency determination.
The clinical safety owner defines immediate-danger, ambiguous, third-party, refusal, disconnect, after-hours and unavailable-responder procedures, including lawful disclosures and jurisdictions.
The runtime supports configurable per-procedure behaviour (third-party concern, caller refusal, disconnect, after-hours, unavailable responder) once procedures are approved.
Route selection comes from trusted allowlisted queues/destinations.
Route selection uses actual service hours and capacity of the destinations.
Never dial arbitrary user-, model- or document-supplied numbers.
External emergency/crisis contact requires an approved operational protocol, geography, consent or legal basis, minimum disclosure and a failed-connection procedure (never automated by keyword).
Transfer event model REQUESTED, QUEUED, RECEIVER_ACCEPTED, BRIDGED, CALLER_CONFIRMED_CONNECTED, COMPLETED plus timeout/failure/disconnect.
Persist authenticated provider transfer events with event ids and causal timestamps.
Accept duplicate and out-of-order delivery and derive state only when prerequisites are evidenced.

Fault matrix denominator and gate: the fixed fault registry (the 25 plans in scenarios/fixtures/failures plus every prompt section 17 fault-matrix item, 50 fault ids, rows FO-17-24.<FAULT_ID>) is the denominator; every id has a plan, an injection point and a reached-and-asserted run, and an uninjectable or unreached fault is a coverage hole, never PASS.

Fault matrix AUTH_EXPIRY_IDLE: Auth expires while idle. The fault is injected at its real injection point (session idle expiry (lastActivityAt) in the identity service and the DynamoDB session store), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix AUTH_EXPIRY_DURING_SPEECH: Auth expires during speech. The fault is injected at its real injection point (emission-time session re-check at the audio release boundary), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix AUTH_EXPIRY_MID_CALL: Session expires between prepare and commit. The fault is injected at its real injection point (session expiry between prepare and commit (injected clock)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix DELEGATION_REVOKED: Revoked delegation. The fault is injected at its real injection point (relationship-directory revocation while work is pending (recheck under durable grants)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix CONSENT_REVOKED: Revoked consent. The fault is injected at its real injection point (consent-registry revocation during a call and while work is pending), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix CONCURRENT_SAME_ACCOUNT: Two concurrent calls change the same appointment. The fault is injected at its real injection point (a second call commits to the same record while the first awaits confirmation (two gateway sessions on two postgres:16 connections with the WP-04 race helper, against the WP-23 reference business API; never PGlite)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix CHANGED_SLOT_DURING_CONFIRMATION: Changed slot during confirmation. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the scheduling source changes the slot version between read-back and commit), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix INTERRUPTED_CONFIRMATION: Caller barges in during the confirmation prompt. The fault is injected at its real injection point (barge-in during the confirmation read-back at the audio boundary), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix STALE_SOURCE: Stale source. The fault is injected at its real injection point (a context source older than its freshness budget (warehouse snapshot older than a payment)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix CONTRADICTORY_EVENT: Contradictory event. The fault is injected at its real injection point (two sources or events disagree on a field used by the snapshot), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix EVENTS_OUT_OF_ORDER: Transfer events arrive out of order. The fault is injected at its real injection point (carrier transfer events delivered out of order to the carrier_event_inbox), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix DUPLICATE_WEBHOOK: Vendor redelivers the same event twice. The fault is injected at its real injection point (inbound inbox redelivery with the same (tenant, source, event_id) and outbox redelivery), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix MISSING_WEBHOOK: Missing webhook. The fault is injected at its real injection point (a vendor event that never arrives (Talkdesk/Salesforce emulator drops it)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix SCHEDULING_TIMEOUT_AFTER_COMMIT: Scheduling commit times out after it was applied. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the reference business API applies the change and times out the response), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix CRASH_AFTER_COMMIT: Process crashes after the external system committed. The fault is injected at its real injection point (worker process death between the provider commit and the ledger record (two workers on postgres:16)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix RECEIPT_LOST: Lost receipt. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the commit receipt or completion event never arrives), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix RECEIPT_LATE: Late receipt. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the receipt arrives after the reconcile budget or after a newer turn), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix SALESFORCE_OUTAGE: Salesforce unavailable during case creation. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the Salesforce emulator refuses connections for the whole call), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix SCHEMA_DRIFT: Drifted schema. The fault is injected at its real injection point (a connector response or metadata whose fields differ from the profile mapping), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix DLQ_FULL: Full DLQ. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the dead-letter destination is at capacity or unwritable (ElasticMQ)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix MODEL_REFUSAL: Model refusal. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the model emulator returns a provider refusal), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix MODEL_HANG: Model hang. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the model stream stalls past its deadline), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix MODEL_OVERLOAD: Model overload. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the model emulator returns overload/rate-limit errors), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix ASR_FAILURE: ASR failure. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the ASR sidecar or managed ASR fails or returns no partials), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix TTS_FAILURE: TTS failure. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the TTS sidecar or managed TTS fails mid-utterance), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix JUDGE_FAILURE: Judge failure. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the pre-release or monitor judge times out or errors), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix RECEIVER_UNAVAILABLE: No human receiver available. The fault is injected at its real injection point (no staffed receiver accepts within the attempt window), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix RECEIVER_DECLINED: Human declines. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the receiver client declines the transfer), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix TRANSFER_FAILED: Transfer to the first destination fails. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the first allowlisted destination rejects the transfer), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix BRIDGE_DROPPED: Bridge drops after receiver acceptance. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the bridge drops after receiver acceptance (LiveKit/SIP warm transfer)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix RECORDING_REFUSED: Recording refusal. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the caller declines recording on the media path), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix AUDIT_OUTAGE: Durable audit evidence cannot be written. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the central sink and local audit outbox cannot be written (MinIO Object Lock and Postgres in Layer 2)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix LOCAL_PERSISTENCE_FAILURE: Local persistence failure. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the primary database write fails (postgres:16 stopped or read-only)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix REDACTION_FAILURE: Redaction of a transcript fails. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the redaction stage fails on a transcript segment), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix SOURCE_DELETED: Source deletion. The fault is injected at its real injection point (a subject or source record is deleted while work is pending), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix SOURCE_MERGED: Source merge. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the identity directory merges two subjects), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix SOURCE_SPLIT: Source split. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the identity directory splits one subject into two), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix REGIONAL_FAILOVER: Primary region fails during a call. The fault is injected at its real injection point (regional uncertainty with the application write fence (FO-16-44a)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix QUOTA_EXHAUSTED: AI or budget quota exhausted mid-call. The fault is injected at its real injection point (vendor or AI quota exhausted mid-call (shared quota counters)), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: Budget exhaustion. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the spend ledger reaches a tenant/cohort/model ceiling mid-call), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix BILLING_TIMEOUT: Billing system times out on read. The fault is injected at its real injection point (reference business API billing read timeout), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix CLAIMS_TIMEOUT: Claims system times out. The fault is injected at its real injection point (reference business API claims read timeout), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix PROVIDER_API_TIMEOUT: Provider network API times out. The fault is injected at its real injection point (reference business API provider-network timeout before send), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix SCHEDULING_UNAVAILABLE: Scheduling system unavailable on read. The fault is injected at its real injection point (reference business API scheduling read refused before send), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix PARTIAL_WRITE: Dependency reports a partial write. The fault is injected at its real injection point (reference business API applies the first step of a multi-step write then fails), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix KNOWLEDGE_STALE: Matching article is expired. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the only matching approved article expires or is superseded), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix IDP_UNAVAILABLE: Identity provider unavailable. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the OIDC provider (Keycloak) is unavailable during secure-link approval), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix NOTIFICATION_PROVIDER_DOWN: Notification provider unavailable. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the email/SMS sender (Mailpit/LocalStack) is unavailable), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix POLICY_ENGINE_ERROR: Policy evaluation errors. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the in-process OPA evaluation throws or is undefined), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Fault matrix GUARDRAIL_LIMIT: Refusal / turn limit reached in a crisis conversation. The fault is injected at its real injection point (the conversation guard reaches its refusal count or turn limit during a safety interaction), the run proves the fault point was reached, and the postconditions are asserted.

Input/output monitors: ASR entity accuracy, uncertainty, language support, intent routing, prompt injection, scope, minimization, retrieved-source relevance, stale/unsupported facts, commitments, authorization, false completion/transfer, stigma/sycophancy, loops, inappropriate reassurance, safety-routing outcomes.
Deterministic checks for facts/actions plus qualified semantic judges at each model input and output boundary, including tool and TTS outputs.
Judges need test sets, blind human labels, severity definitions, precision/recall, sensitivity/specificity with confidence intervals, calibration and drift checks.
Include a random sample of unflagged conversations to estimate missed cases.
Separate generator and judge model families when feasible; human adjudication resolves material disagreements.
Judge scores cannot prove external effects, caller authority or accepted human connection.
Usable support routing availability >=99.95% monthly end to end.
Warm simple turn latency p50 <=800 ms, p95 <=1.5 s (goal 500 ms/1 s) from end of caller speech to first meaningful handset audio; cold starts, acknowledgments and tool-backed turns separate.
Healthy-dependency tool-backed meaningful response p95 <=3 s.
Interruption stop p95 <=250 ms from detected interruption to last handset audio; separately report onset -> detection -> stop.
100% protected actions/utterances have valid checks; all accepted consequential actions have durable audit; zero duplicate effects in required failure tests.
CRM synchronization >=99.9% within 60 s under normal dependencies; outage backlog and recovery reported separately.
>=99.5% accepted transfer attempts connect when a receiver is available; publish all attempts, unavailable/declined receivers and failed connections.
>=95% verified goal completion per supported routine launch intent under declared conditions; no critical failure; no blending unsupported requests or eligibility relabeling.
Human warmth/clarity >=4/5 (goal 4.3) with predeclared rubric, reviewer count, uncertainty and unacceptable subgroup outcomes.
Any critical privacy/authorization/clinical-boundary/effect failure blocks the affected release regardless of averages or cost.
Publish p50/p95/p99 by intent/language/audience/assurance/model/voice/load/region with sample counts, exclusions, missing observations and confidence intervals.
Report ASR important-entity error and WER; completion latency, total silence, interruptions, backchannel selectivity and user effort.
Finite zero observed errors never proves zero risk (~3/n bound); related simulations are not n independent people.
